# create-scifr

create-scifr is a scaffolding tool for building SCIFR projects. SCIFR (Self-Contained Interactive Single File Report) is a design pattern for turning a React + Vite single-page application into one portable HTML file with a data payload embedded at a stable boundary inside the HTML. This makes it well-suited for bioinformatics and data science pipelines, where tools like Snakemake, Nextflow, or custom scripts can produce a structured output file and inject it directly into a SCIFR template to produce a shareable interactive report — with no server, no CDN, and no internet connection required.

SCIFR is initially described in a preprint: "Interactive data analysis and reporting with SCIFR: A Single-File SPA Approach" (bioRxiv, 2025, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.07.10.664259). The pattern was later applied as the enabling design in BLITSFR (BLAST Interactive Tracks Single-File Report), published in *Bioinformatics Advances*, Vol 6 Issue 1, 2026 (DOI: https://doi.org/10.1093/bioadv/vbag282), for enabling efficient interactive comparison of large numbers of sequences.

## Design

The SCIFR design is inspired by plasmid cloning. In molecular biology, a plasmid is commonly used as a template for transferring a particular DNA sequence into a new experiment — the plasmid provides a stable, reusable scaffold while the insert changes. A SCIFR is the software equivalent: a self-contained interactive report that travels independently of any server or infrastructure. The `<script id="scifr-data">` data boundary acts as the integration site that tools can target to inject or replace data without touching the surrounding application code. The `mutate-scifr` CLI is the restriction enzyme.

## Getting started

```
npx create-scifr my-project
cd my-project
npm run dev
```

This scaffolds a new project and starts the webapp development server. A demo project is created automatically on first launch using the bundled Iris dataset, so the app is immediately interactive.

## Two modes

A SCIFR project has two distinct build outputs and runtime modes.

**Webapp mode** runs the app as a full interactive web application with IndexedDB-backed project management. It can be used to load data, explore visualisations, save project snapshots, and export finished reports. This is useful when you want to give users a persistent project workspace — hosted somewhere, they can load a SCIFR payload, interact with it, save their work, and return to it later. Run with `npm run dev` or build with `npm run build:app`, which produces `dist/index.html`.

**Template mode** produces a self-contained single-file HTML report — `dist/scifr.html` — with demo data in its data boundary. A pipeline can replace that payload to generate the final report. Built with `npm run build:scifr`. Data injection can be done using the `mutate-scifr` CLI or any language or script that can manipulate HTML strings.

The two modes are complementary. Use the webapp when you want users to have a flexible, persistent workspace for exploring payloads. Use the template and CLI in automated pipelines.

## Project structure

A scaffolded project has two HTML entry points:

- `index.html` — loads the webapp via `src/index.jsx` → `App.jsx`
- `scifr.html` — loads the template viewer via `src/scifr.jsx` → `ScifrApp.jsx`

And three Vite config files:

- `vite.config.mjs` — webapp build
- `vite.scifr.config.mjs` — template build (`emptyOutDir: false`, input = `scifr.html`)
- `vite.shared.mjs` — shared config factory (React plugin, `__SCIFR_VERSION__` define, 100MB asset inline limit)

The key source files are:

```
src/
  App.jsx               webapp root — project management, export, snapshot save/restore
  ScifrApp.jsx          template viewer — reads the DOM payload, renders Main read-only
  store.js              all Jotai atoms: project atoms and UI state atoms
  scifrReport.js        buildScifrDownload(): fetch template, pack snapshot, trigger download
  loadScifrData.js      loadScifrData() + unpackPayload(): read and decompress scifr-data boundary
  scifrExampleData.js   Iris dataset helpers used by the demo chapter
  input.columnar.gzip.base64.json  bundled demo seed data (columnar + gzip + base64)
  db/
    index.js            opens the IndexedDB database (scifr-db, projects store)
    projects.js         CRUD operations: createProject, updateProjectSnapshot,
                        updateLastBackedUpAt, importAllProjects, exportAllProjects
  hooks/
    useProjects.js      React hook wrapping all db operations with Jotai project atoms
    useSnapshot.js      capture(): reads all UI atoms into a snapshot object
                        restore(): writes atom values back from a stored snapshot
  components/
    Main.jsx            the slide deck renderer; receives scifrData, onProjectsClick, onSaveProject
    ScifrNav.jsx        top navigation bar with GitHub link, active project name, Save, Projects
    ProjectPanel.jsx    DaisyUI modal for project management: create, import, rename,
                        delete, backup, restore, and export
    IrisExampleChapter.jsx  interactive Iris scatter plot chapter (the demo visualisation)
    WhatIsScifrChapter.jsx, ArchitectureChapter.jsx,
    BoilerplateChapter.jsx, MutationWorkflowChapter.jsx  informational handbook chapters
```

## Data and snapshots

Each project stores a snapshot in IndexedDB. The snapshot has two fields:

```json
{
  "data": { "scifrExampleInputJSON": { "irisData": [...] } },
  "uiState": {
    "nodeSize": 8,
    "isInteractive": true,
    "colorScheme": "nivo",
    "legendPosition": "bottom-right",
    "legendOffsetX": 120,
    "legendOffsetY": 0
  }
}
```

`data` holds the domain payload — whatever the application renders. `uiState` holds all Jotai UI atom values so that switching between projects fully restores the visual state, not just the data. Legacy snapshots without a `data` field are handled transparently via `snapshot?.data ?? snapshot`.

### Save and load cycle

When the user clicks Save Project, `useSnapshot.capture(scifrData)` reads all current atom values and packages them alongside the data into `{ data, uiState }`, which is written to IndexedDB. When a project is loaded or switched, `useSnapshot.restore(snapshot)` writes all the atom values back, and `scifrData` is updated to `activeProject?.snapshot?.data ?? activeProject?.snapshot ?? null`, which flows into `Main` as a prop.

### HTML export cycle

Clicking Export HTML calls `buildScifrDownload({ snapshot, title })`. It wraps the snapshot in a report envelope:

```json
{ "format": "scifr", "version": 1, "metadata": { ... }, "snapshot": { ... } }
```

The envelope is gzip-compressed and base64-encoded, then injected into `dist/scifr.html` by replacing the `<script id="scifr-data">` boundary content. The result is downloaded as `<title>.html`. This requires a production build — the check for external script `src` attributes prevents the export from running against the dev server.

### Template viewer read cycle

When a SCIFR report is opened in a browser, `ScifrApp` calls `loadScifrData()`, which reads the `<script id="scifr-data">` element from the DOM, then calls `unpackPayload()` to base64-decode and gunzip the content. If the result has `format === 'scifr'`, the viewer uses `data.snapshot` — this is the webapp export path. If there is no `format` field, the data is used directly — this is the `mutate-scifr` CLI path, kept for backward compatibility.

## Data boundary

All SCIFR payloads are embedded in HTML as:

```html
<script id="scifr-data" type="application/json">
{"startIdx":"scifr-data-start","payload":<packed>,"endIdx":"scifr-data-end"}
</script>
```

The `payload` field is a gzip+base64 packed object for webapp exports, or a columnar packed object for CLI outputs. Uncompressed plain JSON also works — `unpackPayload` handles both.

## CLI injection

```
npx mutate-scifr --data mydata.csv --template dist/scifr.html --output report.html
```

The CLI accepts `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.tab`, and `.json`. It injects a plain data payload without a report envelope.

The Node.js CLI is the reference implementation, but the mutation is simple enough to reimplement in any language. The only requirement is to locate the `<script id="scifr-data">` tag and replace its text content.

```python
# Python
import json, gzip, base64, re

def mutate_scifr(template_path, payload, output_path):
    compressed = gzip.compress(json.dumps(payload).encode())
    packed = {"format_version": 1, "compression": "gzip", "encoding": "base64",
              "payload": base64.b64encode(compressed).decode()}
    envelope = json.dumps({"startIdx": "scifr-data-start", "payload": packed,
                           "endIdx": "scifr-data-end"})
    html = open(template_path).read()
    result = re.sub(r'(<script id="scifr-data"[^>]*>)(.*?)(</script>)',
                    lambda m: m.group(1) + envelope + m.group(3), html, flags=re.DOTALL)
    open(output_path, 'w').write(result)
```

```r
# R
mutate_scifr <- function(template_path, payload, output_path) {
  library(jsonlite); library(base64enc)
  compressed <- memCompress(toJSON(payload, auto_unbox=TRUE), type="gzip")
  envelope <- toJSON(list(startIdx="scifr-data-start",
    payload=list(format_version=1, compression="gzip", encoding="base64",
                 payload=base64encode(compressed)),
    endIdx="scifr-data-end"), auto_unbox=TRUE)
  html <- paste(readLines(template_path), collapse="\n")
  result <- gsub('(<script id="scifr-data"[^>]*>)(.*?)(</script>)',
                 paste0("\\1", envelope, "\\3"), html, perl=TRUE)
  writeLines(result, output_path)
}
```

## File formats

Three file formats are used across the SCIFR workflow:

| Extension | Contents |
|---|---|
| `.html` | Self-contained SCIFR report. The full application and data are inlined. gzip+base64 payload embedded at the scifr-data boundary. |
| `.scifr` | Single project export: `{ format, version, name, exportedAt, snapshot }`. Plain JSON. |
| `.scifr.projects` | Bulk backup bundle: `{ exportedAt, version, projects: [...] }`. Plain JSON. |

## Project management

The Projects modal (opened from the nav bar) provides the full project lifecycle:

- **New project** accepts an optional data file seed (`.scifr` or `.json`) so the project starts with data rather than empty.
- **Import Project** loads a `.scifr` or `.json` file as a new project. It detects and rejects backup files, redirecting to Restore Backup instead.
- **Backup Projects** exports all projects as a `.scifr.projects` bundle and stamps `lastBackedUpAt` on each project.
- **Restore Backup** imports a `.scifr.projects` bundle. If a project exists locally with a newer `updatedAt`, it is skipped.
- Each project in the list shows a backup age indicator: green under 3 days, yellow 3–7 days, red over 7 days.
- Per-project actions: Save, Export `.scifr`, Export HTML, Rename, Delete.

## Extending the boilerplate

**To add a new chapter**, create `src/components/MyChapter.jsx` and export a config object and a default component:

```jsx
export const myChapterConfig = { id: 'my-chapter', title: 'My Chapter' };

export default function MyChapter({ active }) {
  return <section data-chapter-id={myChapterConfig.id} className="scifr-slide">...</section>;
}
```

Then import it and add it to the `chapters` array in `Main.jsx`. The component receives `active` (boolean, true when the slide is in view) and any `componentProps` defined alongside it in the array.

**To add new UI state to the project snapshot**, add a Jotai atom to `store.js`, then add a corresponding `useAtom` read/write pair to `useSnapshot.js` — include the value in `capture()` and the setter call in `restore()`. The atom is then saved and restored automatically on every project save and switch.

## Stack

SCIFR is a design pattern, not a framework. The stack in this boilerplate is a personal choice based on familiarity — other developers can implement the same pattern with Vue, Svelte, Angular, or any other SPA toolchain. What matters is that the build produces a single self-contained HTML file with a stable `<script id="scifr-data">` boundary. Everything else is up to the developer.

The choices made here, and why:

- **React** renders the viewer interface. Components receive the unpacked data payload as props and render charts, tables, or whatever the report needs.
- **Vite** handles the build. Its `viteSingleFile` plugin inlines all JS and CSS assets into the HTML, which is what makes the output truly self-contained. The dual-config setup (`vite.config.mjs` and `vite.scifr.config.mjs`) separates the webapp build from the template build.
- **Jotai** holds shared reactive state across components — chart controls, navigation, UI settings. Its atom model maps cleanly to the `uiState` field in the project snapshot, making per-project state save/restore straightforward.
- **Tailwind CSS + DaisyUI** handle styling. DaisyUI provides ready-made components (modals, buttons, badges, collapse) so the project panel UI stays concise without custom CSS.
- **Nivo** provides the demo scatter plot. Any charting library works here — Nivo was chosen because it is React-native, responsive, and reasonably lightweight for a bundled report.
- **idb** is a thin wrapper around the browser's IndexedDB API. It handles the webapp's project storage — each project record holds a name, timestamps, backup metadata, and the full snapshot.

## Build commands

```
npm run dev          # start the webapp dev server
npm run build        # run build:app then build:scifr sequentially
npm run build:app    # outputs dist/index.html (the webapp)
npm run build:scifr  # outputs dist/scifr.html (the template)
npm run preview      # preview the production webapp build
```
